trust_decision.summary: Whether a client-supplied column/identifier name (query param `field`) may be spliced verbatim into SQL via MyBatis ${} substitution; decided nowhere at the pinned commit: mapField falls back to the raw input and the XML mappers interpolate it.

landing_point.why: Summary names `${field}` interpolation in a MyBatis mapper for the analysis endpoint; grep for ${field} lands in the HistoryMapper.xml files (three dialects), then back to PBHMetricsController.handleHistoryNumberAccess.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Published fix is a single SqlInjectionUtils.check in the controller (fix.diff:26-28); no other module touched.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The ORDER BY routes take a different parameter (`orderBy`, not `field`), a different mapper (PeerRecordMapper.xml), different controllers (PBHChartController, PBHPeerController) and are gated by Role.PBH_PLUS, so a solver can argue they are a neighbouring sort feature, not the 'analysis field' injection the report describes.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate dto-style and camelCase names must keep working: field=peerId/peer_id triggers the substring(8) branch, camelCase is converted to snake_case and aliased (torrentName->t.name joins torrents); orderBy accepts `name|desc` and dto names remapped to columns, with unknown names passed through as-is. An allowlist that omits the camelCase/dotted mapped forms, or that rejects the `|desc` suffix, breaks charts and sortable tables.

O6_input_shapes: single string query param `field` (plain identifier vs. SQL fragment), checked by MyBatis-Plus SqlInjectionUtils.check (keyword/comment blacklist)

O7_producer.where: src/main/java/com/ghostchu/peerbanhelper/util/query/Orderable.java:74-85 (generateOrderBy builds the raw ORDER BY string from user `orderBy` params, remapping.getOrDefault falls back to raw input) consumed by ${orderBySql} at src/main/resources/mapper/sqlite/PeerRecordMapper.xml:32,51

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different parameter (sort), different controller and mapper; PBH_PLUS-gated chart, looks like a separate feature from the field-analysis endpoint.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different controller file and mapper XML; Orderable in util.query package

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Peer-detail page sorting, not analysis; reaches SQL through a service that hides the raw string behind an Orderable object.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another controller, service impl, and mapper XML (x3 dialects: sqlite/mysql/postgres)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Same three ${field}/${orderBySql} sinks duplicated per dialect (mysql, postgres, sqlite mapper dirs); service-level HistoryService.countField/sumField remain unchecked if called by any other caller
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Only controller caller today; dialect copies fall together with one service-level fix.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Orderable.apply feeds raw user column names into MyBatis-Plus QueryWrapper.orderBy for ban logs, torrent lists, swarm tracking (PBHBanController.java:124, PBHTorrentController.java:87,131,174, SwarmTrackingModule.java:88); whether MP 3.5.16 validates these columns is unverified, so a planted unchecked variant is realistic.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same helper already produces raw ORDER BY text; maintainers treat sort keys as harmless metadata.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: statsSortField currently picks a constant table name; a variant concatenating the user value into queryWrapper.last(...) would be a natural how-type sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The comment block shows maintainers deliberately use raw `last()` SQL for stats sorting.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: /api/statistic/analysis/date currently switches on field; a version passing field to a ${field} date mapper would be realistic.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Sibling handler in same controller takes the same `field` param.

O9_family: SQL injection (CWE-89) via MyBatis ${} identifier substitution (SELECT-list/WHERE and ORDER BY positions)
